key_insight: In older postmenopausal women, menopausal timing showed a nonlinear association with blood NfL and a linear association with GDF-15, offering clues to links between reproductive aging and dementia-related biology.
clinical_relevance: These observational biomarker findings may inform dementia research but do not establish dementia risk prediction or support changes in clinical care.
method: Analyzed U.S. Health and Retirement Study participants aged 65 or older using blood collected in 2016.
Modeled self-reported spontaneous menopause timing against NfL, GFAP, p-tau181 and GDF-15, adjusting for sociodemographic and health factors.
Evaluated APOE ε4 effect modification and examined hysterectomy history in secondary analyses.
evidence_signal: Among 893 women without hysterectomy, later menopause between ages 50–55 was associated with lower NfL (−0.031 SD/year; 95% CI, −0.051 to −0.011); GFAP and p-tau181 associations were not significant.
watch_item: Self-reported reproductive history and observational biomarker associations cannot establish causality or demonstrate effects on dementia incidence.
paper_title: Age at Menopause and Dementia Risk: Blood-Based Biomarker Evidence from a US National Study
